name: nm50
question: Does nm25 re-trained with a size head (fold, call, raise or all-in, then a raise size scored as a function of the size, trained on 8 sizes drawn at random every decision and played on a 16-size grid), with nm25's recipe otherwise unchanged, play at least as well as nm25 while betting sizes nm25 cannot, and give away no more about its hand through its sizes?
why: Bet sizing, plan B (docs/2026-11-23-review-and-plan.md, section 6; requested 2026-11-27): a network that scores any size instead of choosing among three. The size head (ninemax_selfplay.SizeHeadNet; docs/2026-11-17-model-mathematics.md) starts as a size-head copy of nm25 distilled on nm25's own play (ninemax_sizehead_init.py, run by the pipeline before training: a 300-step copy read -0.38 [-1.29, +0.54] bb/100 against nm25 offered nm25's sizes and +1.03 [+0.10, +1.95] on the 16-size grid). Training offers 8 sizes drawn log-uniformly afresh every decision (size8: opens 2-4bb, re-raises 2-4x, bets and raises 0.2-3 pot) with the rule players on nm25's menu; it is judged on the grid16 menu, which Kestrel plays (its C++ reproduces a size-head network exactly). Every check was run end to end at small size on a 3-minute size-head network. nm48 asks the same about a fixed wider menu; this run asks it about a continuous one.

checks.why: it must not lose to nm25 in nm25's own game, at a table where each plays its own menu
nm45's check: on the same deals as nm25, the 95% interval of the difference must lie above -2.0 bb/100 against every rule player
at least as good as nm25 on average across 25 generated players, and never far behind
bluff jams and raises must lose prize equity against it, as against nm25
as nm45 and nm48: the mean of four 30-minute exploiters (which play its menu and so every size it offers); limit nm25's +0.75 plus 0.5
a report: which sizes of the grid it uses and where, and how much its sizes say about its hand against nm25's
